text:
sasha: quick heads-up — brought up the new 'marlin-lite-v2' embed in staging, running the standard recall+k and clustering checks. noticed odd density gap on a few shards.

mike: density gap? can you paste the plot or numbers?

sasha: attaching quick ascii summary here — shard A has avg norm 0.87, shard B 0.43, cluster silhouette dropped from 0.62 -> 0.48 on short queries.

jordana: could be a tokenization/normalization mismatch during offline build. last time we saw that with a model that used different whitespace handling.

priyanka: also check nearest-neighbor distance distribution (k=10). if there's a long tail it inflates avg norms.

(eval-bot): ran quick eval: recall@1=0.71, recall@10=0.92, mean_cosine_shardA=0.86, mean_cosine_shardB=0.44, silhouette=0.49. full report: https://ci/reports/4456789012/marlin-lite-v2 (staging).

sasha: thanks — recall numbers look ok overall but shard variance is concerning for production rollouts. i re-ran with the exact same preprocessing used in prod -> still gap.

mike: can you share the sample that exhibits the gap? maybe it's concentrated on long documents or non-en.

sasha: sample split by length: short (<128 tokens) recall@1 = 0.74, mid = 0.69, long(>1024) = 0.61. distribution skewed toward short, but shardB aligned with long docs.

jordana: suggestion — run a spectral-gap test on the affinity matrix to see if clusters are collapsing. command i use: 
```
python eval/embed_diag.py --model marlin-lite-v2 --dataset staging-sample --metrics recall silhouette spectral_gap --k 10
```

priyanka: also try whitening + L2 normalize before knn to see if it reduces shard effect. remember our previous patch: `whiten=True, l2norm=True` helped with multi-domain mixes.

mike: curious about quantization impact — is this int4 quantized run? sometimes per-channel vs per-tensor shifts cause weird norms.

sasha: this was fp16 baseline. we'll test int4 next. planning to run int4-perchannel and int4-pertensor.

(eval-bot): queued job 4456789123: quant runs (int4-perch, int4-pert) scheduled on gpu-pool-staging. ETA ~20m.

jordana: small note — when comparing recall delta please compute recall_delta = new - baseline and show confidence intervals with bootstrap (n=500). short tails can flip numbers.

priyanka: would be great to get a pairwise trace for a few failure cases. suffix example: ||query|| -> top1 vs baseline top1. that helps pinpoint whether vectors moved uniformly or just neighbors permuted.

sasha: compiling pairwise diffs now. preliminary: 8/50 sampled failures show nearest neighbor swapped with a semantically unrelated doc -> suggests embedding collapse for that subdomain.

mike: can you run UMAP 2D with color by shard and by document length? quick visual often reveals whether it's a normalization or data issue.

sasha: doing UMAP now. will paste link.

(eval-bot): quant runs complete. int4-perchannel recall@1=0.69 (-0.02), recall@10=0.90 (-0.02), silhouette=0.45 (-0.04). int4-pertensor recall@1=0.66 (-0.05), recall@10=0.88 (-0.04), silhouette=0.40 (-0.09). full artifacts: https://ci/reports/4456789123/quant-compare

jordana: ok int4-perchannel looks acceptable delta-wise, per-tensor much worse. that suggests per-channel quant is the path if we want smaller model.

priyanka: also add an eval on cross-lingual samples — we saw earlier that quantization amplifies idiosyncrasies on non-en text.

mike: next steps proposal: 1) run whitening+L2 + int4-perchannel 2) rerun spectral-gap and bootstrap CIs 3) generate top-1 pairwise diffs for 200 failure candidates 4) check on holdout multi-lang subset.

sasha: agreed. i'll kick off 1 & 2 now. allocating a longer run for 3.

jordana: if whitening fixes shardB norms, we should consider adding whitening to the default prod pipeline for this model family. add an opt-in flag first.

sasha: noted. will keep this thread updated with results. tl;dr: marlin-lite-v2 staging shows a shard density gap; int4-perchannel is promising; whitening + l2norm is first mitigation to test. :white_check_mark:
